evaluation-plan.why: Specifies a 150-note golden set with diversity requirements, dual annotators with adjudication, explicit numeric bars on recall/precision/owner accuracy/date accuracy/latency/cost, an LLM-as-judge secondary rubric, and multiple online signals (acceptance rate, edit rate, deletion rate, re-run rate) with steady-state targets. Comprehensive and concrete.

graceful-fallback.why: Section 6 is cut off mid-sentence so the full fallback behavior is not described. The document references it repeatedly and lists trigger conditions, but the actual user experience during fallback is not shown in the candidate output.

failure-modes-guardrails.why: Enumerates 8 AI-specific failure modes including hallucinated items, missed items, wrong owner, garbled dates, context-window overflow, and confident-but-wrong output. Each is paired with a concrete detection method (source_span validation, golden-set metrics, edit signals) and a specific mitigation (span suppression, editable chips, absolute date display, no silent truncation).

non-ai-baseline.why: Explicitly describes the non-AI baseline (structured template), explains why it fails in practice, articulates why AI earns its place (free-form prose requires language understanding), and keeps the manual template as a permanent fallback. Includes a concrete threshold below which the baseline is the better decision.

uncertainty-and-reversibility.why: UI presents output as reviewable suggestions ('Review these suggestions'), low-confidence owners are editable chips visually distinguished, absolute dates shown alongside source text, 'Did we miss anything?' affordance, and users can edit or delete individual items before accepting. Human-in-the-loop is explicit throughout.

cost-latency.why: P95 latency target of ≤6 seconds and cost target of ≤$0.02 per extraction at p95 note length are both explicit gate criteria that must be met simultaneously before canary rollout.

success-metrics-multi-dimensional.why: Quality metrics (recall, precision, owner accuracy, date accuracy) are paired with adoption/outcome metrics (acceptance rate ≥70%, deletion rate ≤15%, edit rate, re-run rate) and operational guardrails (latency, cost). Spans multiple dimensions with explicit targets.

staged-rollout.why: Canary is mentioned as the first post-evaluation destination and §10 references gate-2 decisions, but the full staged rollout plan (shadow mode, canary size/duration, GA criteria, kill switch mechanism) is not elaborated in the visible text.
